questions.question: How does Ezekiel 16 portray Jerusalem?
options: As a very wealthy merchant who traded freely with all the kingdoms of the whole wide world
As a mighty and exalted queen who ruled in peace over very many distant nations
As an abandoned infant whom God rescued, raised, and married, but who became unfaithful
As a wholly faithful bride who never once left the side of her own beloved husband
questions.answer: As an abandoned infant whom God rescued, raised, and married, but who became unfaithful

questions.question: Despite the unfaithfulness, what does God promise at the end of chapter 16?
options: To hand her over entirely to all of the surrounding hostile nations
To wait patiently until she had at last earned back all of his favor
To cast her off entirely and forever without any pity or any mercy
To remember his covenant and establish an everlasting covenant
questions.answer: To remember his covenant and establish an everlasting covenant

questions.question: Ezekiel 16 compares Jerusalem's sin to that of her 'sisters' Samaria and Sodom.
When I passed by you and saw you wallowing in your blood, I said to you, '_____!'
But you trusted in your _____ and played the whore because of your renown.
